# Test fixtures

Generated by `npx ts-node scripts/make-fixtures.ts` — **do not hand-edit them**, regenerate
instead. They are checked in so the exact bytes under test are reviewable in a diff and so the
suite never regenerates them at run time.

| file | what it exercises |
|---|---|
| `with-exif.jpg` | a photo carrying real camera EXIF: `Make`/`Model`, `DateTimeOriginal`, GPS 36.632 / 4.205 (the seeded Kabylie wildfire case) |
| `no-exif.jpg` | the same pixels without the APP1 segment — `exifr` returns `undefined`, which the trust pipeline must treat as `ok: null` |
| `recompressed.jpg` | the EXIF-bearing photo re-encoded at quality 62 — a dHash must still match it, and the EXIF must survive |
| `resized.jpg` | the same photo at 320×320 — a dHash must survive the resize |
| `different.jpg` | a different image — a dHash must **not** match it |

## Why the EXIF is hand-written

`exifr` reads EXIF; nothing here needs to *write* it except the fixture generator, and an
EXIF-writing dependency is not worth adding for that. `scripts/make-fixtures.ts` therefore builds
the APP1 segment by hand: a little-endian TIFF with IFD0 (Make, Model, DateTime), an **Exif
sub-IFD** (DateTimeOriginal) and a **GPS sub-IFD** (two references plus three rationals per
coordinate).

Two mistakes were made and then fixed while building it, worth knowing about:

1. `DateTimeOriginal` (`0x9003`) belongs in the **Exif sub-IFD**, not in IFD0. In IFD0 it is
   invisible to `exifr` and to every real camera.
2. The seconds rational must be stored as hundredths (value × 100 with a denominator of 100).
   Writing the raw seconds silently lost ~1.7 km of GPS precision — enough to fail `photoGps`
   for a case near the 2 km threshold.

## Why `withMetadata()` matters

`sharp` **drops all metadata when it re-encodes**. The `recompressed` and `resized` fixtures call
`.withMetadata()` on purpose: without it they would come out EXIF-free, which is precisely the
metadata stripping that `docs/BACKEND_PROMPT.md` §3.5 warns about — a client must never get the
chance to do it before the server has read the EXIF.
